name: PixiTween Director S11: the director as an MCP server (Option A)
description: Offline PRD for the optional S11 stretch, Option A: expose the director over MCP (Streamable HTTP, stateless, passcode-protected) with five tools (create_film, get_film, edit_film, list_films, get_player_url), SSRF-safe product-image input and a film-service port that is fully testable with an in-memory MCP transport. Option B (Muse Wonder computer use) has no stories: it was researched and recorded as no-go in the design. Mounted through one appended boot hook in server/boot.ts (decision D-3). Start only if S0-S9 are green by Tue 3 Nov 12:00 ET.

Create server/mcp/sdk-smoke.test.ts. userStories.title: Public-address guard for image URLs
userStories.description: As an owner, I want image URLs checked against private address ranges so that the server cannot be tricked into reading internal services.
steps: Read docs/hackathon/steps/step-11-stretch/design.md section 5.2 (the rule table and the blocked ranges) and section 10 (security).

Create server/mcp/ip-guard.ts exporting `class ImageUrlError extends Error { code: 'bad-url' | 'bad-scheme' | 'credentials-in-url' | 'private-address' | 'dns-failed' }`, `isPublicAddress(ip: string): boolean` and `assertPublicHttpsUrl(url: string, lookup: (host: string) => Promise<Array<{ address: string; family: number }>>): Promise<URL>`.

`isPublicAddress` uses `node:net` `isIP`; for IPv4 it rejects the ranges of the design table; for IPv6 it rejects `::`, `::1`, `fc00::/7`, `fe80::/10`, `ff00::/8`, and for IPv4-mapped addresses (`::ffff:a.b.c.d` and the hex form `::ffff:7f00:1`) it re-checks the embedded IPv4 address; an invalid string returns false.

`assertPublicHttpsUrl` rejects an unparseable URL (`bad-url`), any scheme other than `https:` (`bad-scheme`), a URL with a username or password (`credentials-in-url`), an IP-literal host that is not public without calling `lookup` (`private-address`), a host whose lookup throws or returns nothing (`dns-failed`), and a host whose lookup returns any non-public address (`private-address`); otherwise it returns the parsed `URL`.
Create server/mcp/ip-guard.test.ts with the table of addresses below and the URL cases.
acceptanceCriteria: `assertPublicHttpsUrl('http://example.com/a.png', lookup)` rejects with code `bad-scheme`; `https://u:p@example.com/` rejects with `credentials-in-url`; `https://10.0.0.1/` rejects with `private-address` and the injected `lookup` is not called
A host whose lookup returns `[8.8.8.8, 10.0.0.5]` rejects with `private-address`; a host returning `[8.8.8.8]` resolves to a `URL` whose `hostname` is the host
`npm run typecheck` passes
`npm test` passes (offline, no network)
`npm run lint` passes

userStories.title: Product image input: URL fetch and base64 decode
userStories.description: As a client developer, I want the product photo accepted as an https URL or base64 with strict limits so that uploads cannot abuse the server.
steps: Read docs/hackathon/steps/step-11-stretch/design.md section 5.2 (limits, magic bytes, redirects) and server/mcp/ip-guard.ts.

Create server/mcp/image-input.ts exporting `MAX_IMAGE_BYTES = 10 * 1024 * 1024`, `class ImageInputError extends Error { code: 'bad-base64' | 'data-url' | 'too-large' | 'bad-type' | 'bad-status' | 'too-many-redirects' | 'timeout' | 'fetch-failed' }`, `sniffImageMime(bytes: Uint8Array): 'image/png' | 'image/jpeg' | 'image/webp' | undefined` (PNG `89 50 4E 47 0D 0A 1A 0A`; JPEG `FF D8 FF`; WebP `RIFF` + 4 bytes + `WEBP`) and `decodeBase64Image(b64: string): { bytes: Buffer; mime: string }` (rejects a `data:` prefix with `data-url`, invalid base64 with `bad-base64`, more than `MAX_IMAGE_BYTES` with `too-large`, an unknown signature with `bad-type`).

In the same file export `fetchProductImage(url: string, deps: { lookup: Lookup; fetchFn?: typeof fetch; timeoutMs?: number }): Promise<{ bytes: Buffer; mime: string }>`. It calls `assertPublicHttpsUrl` on the URL, fetches with `redirect: 'manual'` and `AbortSignal.timeout(deps.timeoutMs ?? 10000)`, follows at most 3 redirects re-validating each `Location` with `assertPublicHttpsUrl` (a fourth redirect throws `too-many-redirects`), throws `bad-status` for a non-2xx final status, reads the body as a stream and throws `too-large` as soon as the running byte count exceeds `MAX_IMAGE_BYTES`, then checks `sniffImageMime` (`bad-type`). An aborted request throws `timeout`; any other fetch error throws `fetch-failed` with no URL in the message.
Add a code comment that DNS pinning is not implemented (design section 5.2) and that the residual rebinding window is documented in docs/mcp.md.

Create server/mcp/image-input.test.ts with an injected `fetchFn` and `lookup`: a valid PNG, JPEG and WebP; an 11 MB body delivered in 1 MB chunks; a GIF; a 302 to `http://example.com/x`; a 302 to a host whose lookup returns `10.0.0.5`; four chained redirects; a 404; a `fetchFn` that waits for the abort signal with `timeoutMs: 10`.
acceptanceCriteria: `fetchProductImage` returns `{ mime: 'image/png' }` for a body starting with the 8 PNG signature bytes, and `'image/jpeg'` for `FF D8 FF`
An 11 MB streamed body throws `ImageInputError` with code `too-large` after at most 11 chunks are read

A 302 whose `Location` is `http://example.com/x` throws `ImageUrlError` with code `bad-scheme`, and one whose host resolves to `10.0.0.5` throws code `private-address`; four chained redirects throw `too-many-redirects`
`decodeBase64Image('data:image/png;base64,AAAA')` throws code `data-url`; a GIF body (`GIF89a`) throws `bad-type`; a `fetchFn` that never answers with `timeoutMs: 10` throws `timeout`
`npm run typecheck` passes
`npm test` passes (offline, no network)
`npm run lint` passes

userStories.description: As a client developer, I want create_film to return a film id immediately while the director works in the background so that my tool call does not time out.
steps: Read docs/hackathon/steps/step-11-stretch/design.md sections 4, 5.3 and 5.5, docs/hackathon/06-contracts.md sections 3 and 4 (`FilmState`, `FilmStore`, `AssetStore`, `FilmEvent`), server/test-utils/film.ts (`makeTestFilm`) and server/store/film-store.ts.

Create server/mcp/film-service.ts exporting `class ServiceError extends Error { code: 'invalid-input' | 'not-found' | 'not-ready' | 'image-rejected' | 'internal' }`, the interface `McpFilmService { createFilm(input): Promise<CreateFilmResult>; getFilm(filmId): Promise<GetFilmResult>; listFilms(limit): Promise<ListFilmsResult>; editFilm(filmId, message, selection?): Promise<EditFilmResult>; getPlayerUrl(filmId): Promise<GetPlayerUrlResult> }` and `interface ServiceDeps { films: FilmStore; assets: AssetStore; runDirector: (filmId: string) => Promise<void>; runEdit: (filmId: string, message: string, selection?: { sceneId?: string; layerId?: string }, opts?: { local?: boolean }) => Promise<unknown>; subscribe: (filmId: string, fn: (e: FilmEvent) => void) => () => void; emit: (e: FilmEvent) => void; lookup: Lookup; fetchFn?: typeof fetch; publicBaseUrl: string; editWaitMs?: number; now?: () => Date }`.

Export `makeFilmService(deps: ServiceDeps): McpFilmService`. Implement `createFilm`: validate with `createFilmSchema` (`invalid-input`), obtain the bytes through `decodeBase64Image` or `fetchProductImage` (any `ImageUrlError` or `ImageInputError` becomes `image-rejected` with a fixed message that does not echo the URL), `assets.put(bytes, mime, { role: 'product-photo' })`, `films.create({ aspect, brief: { text: brief, productAssetId: asset.id }, assets: [asset], createdAt: (deps.now ?? (() => new Date()))().toISOString() })` (`createdAt` is required since D-12), then start `deps.runDirector(film.id)` without awaiting it.

Attach a `.catch` to the background run that sets the film status to `failed` through `films.update` and emits `{ type: 'error', filmId, at: <ISO time>, where: 'mcp.create_film', message }`. Return `{ filmId, status: 'planning', playerUrl: `${publicBaseUrl}/?film=${filmId}`, note: 'The director is building the film; poll get_film until status is ready.' }`.
Leave `getFilm`, `listFilms`, `editFilm` and `getPlayerUrl` as methods that throw `new Error('not implemented')` for the following stories.
Create server/mcp/film-service.test.ts using `makeTestFilm` stores and a controllable `runDirector` (a deferred promise).
acceptanceCriteria: `createFilm` resolves with `status: 'planning'` and a `playerUrl` ending `/?film=<filmId>` while the `runDirector` promise is still pending
The stored asset has role `product-photo`, the created film's `brief.productAssetId` equals the asset id, and its `createdAt` equals the injected `now()` as an ISO string
A URL whose lookup returns `10.0.0.5` makes `createFilm` reject with `ServiceError` code `image-rejected`, a message that does not contain the hostname, and no film is created
When `runDirector` rejects with `new Error('boom')` the film status becomes `failed` and an `error` event with `where: 'mcp.create_film'` is emitted

userStories.title: Film service: editFilm with a bounded wait
userStories.description: As a client developer, I want edit_film to return when the edit finishes or after a bounded wait so that tool calls do not hang.
steps: Read docs/hackathon/steps/step-11-stretch/design.md section 5.4 (the wait race), docs/hackathon/06-contracts.md section 3 (the `tool.call` event) and server/mcp/film-service.ts.

Implement `editFilm(filmId, message, selection?)` in `makeFilmService`: validate with the `editFilmInput` shapes (`invalid-input`); load the film (`not-found`); if its status is not `ready` throw `ServiceError` `not-ready` with the message `film is still building; poll get_film`.

Subscribe to the film's events with `deps.subscribe` before starting, collecting the `name` of every `tool.call` event with `ok: true`; start `deps.runEdit(filmId, message, selection)`; race it against a timer of `deps.editWaitMs ?? 45000` milliseconds; always unsubscribe in a `finally`.

If the edit finishes first return `{ filmId, done: true, version, appliedTools }` with `version` read from `films.get` after the edit. If the timer wins return `{ filmId, done: false, version, appliedTools: <names so far>, note: 'still running; poll get_film' }` and leave the edit running; a later rejection of the pending edit emits an `error` event with `where: 'mcp.edit_film'` and is never thrown.
A rejection of `runEdit` before the timer throws `ServiceError` `internal` with the message `edit failed`.
Extend server/mcp/film-service.test.ts using vitest fake timers and a fake `subscribe` that lets the test emit `tool.call` events.
acceptanceCriteria: With a fake `runEdit` that emits one `tool.call` event named `setTransform` and resolves, `editFilm` returns `done: true` and `appliedTools: ['setTransform']`
With a `runEdit` that never resolves and `editWaitMs: 45000`, advancing fake timers by 45000 ms makes `editFilm` return `done: false` with the note `still running; poll get_film`
A film with status `building` rejects with `ServiceError` code `not-ready`; an unknown film rejects with `not-found`; the `selection` `{ sceneId: 's2' }` reaches `runEdit` unchanged
The unsubscribe function returned by `subscribe` is called exactly once in the done path and once in the timeout path
`npm run typecheck` passes
`npm test` passes (offline, no network)
`npm run lint` passes

userStories.title: The five MCP tools over an in-memory transport
userStories.description: As an MCP client user, I want five well-described tools so that my assistant can make and edit films.
steps: Read docs/hackathon/steps/step-11-stretch/design.md sections 4, 4.1 (the exact tool descriptions and annotations) and 5.5 (result and error mapping), and server/mcp/film-service.ts.

Create server/mcp/tools.ts exporting `TOOL_NAMES = ['create_film', 'get_film', 'edit_film', 'list_films', 'get_player_url'] as const` and `registerFilmTools(server: McpServer, service: McpFilmService, opts?: { log?: (line: Record<string, unknown>) => void }): void`.

Register each tool with `server.registerTool(name, { title, description, inputSchema, annotations }, callback)`, using the descriptions and annotations of design section 4.1 verbatim and the raw shapes from server/mcp/schemas.ts (`edit_film` passes `sceneId` and `layerId` as the selection).

Each callback returns `{ content: [{ type: 'text', text: JSON.stringify(result) }], structuredContent: result }` on success. A `ServiceError` becomes `{ isError: true, content: [{ type: 'text', text: error.message }] }`. Any other error becomes `{ isError: true, content: [{ type: 'text', text: 'internal error' }] }`. Every call logs `{ event: 'mcp.request', tool, ms, ok }` through `opts.log` (default `console.info` of the JSON string) and never logs arguments or error messages.
Create server/mcp/tools.test.ts: connect a `Client` to a `McpServer` over `InMemoryTransport.createLinkedPair()` with a fake `McpFilmService` and test listing, each call, and the error mapping.
acceptanceCriteria: `client.listTools()` returns exactly the five names of `TOOL_NAMES`, each with a non-empty description, and `get_film`, `list_films` and `get_player_url` have `annotations.readOnlyHint === true`

`callTool` of `create_film` with a fake service returning `{ filmId: 'f1', status: 'planning', playerUrl: 'http://x/?film=f1', note: 'n' }` returns `structuredContent.filmId === 'f1'` and a `content[0].text` that parses to the same object

A fake service that throws `new ServiceError('not-found', 'film not found')` gives `isError: true` and the text `film not found`; one that throws `new Error('boom')` gives `isError: true`, the text `internal error`, and the log line has `ok: false` and does not contain `boom`
A `get_film` call with `filmId: '../x'` either rejects or returns `isError: true`, and the fake service's `getFilm` is not called

`npm test` passes (offline, no network)

userStories.title: The /mcp route: passcode, stateless transport, DNS-rebinding protection
userStories.description: As an owner, I want the MCP endpoint protected by the passcode and served statelessly so that it is safe to expose.
steps: Read docs/hackathon/steps/step-11-stretch/design.md sections 3.1, 5.1, 7 and 10, docs/hackathon/06-contracts.md section 1 (secrets) and server/http/middleware.ts (S2's passcode middleware accepts both header forms; this route checks too).

Create server/mcp-server.ts exporting `checkPasscode(headers: Headers, passcode: string | undefined): boolean` (true when `passcode` is empty or undefined; otherwise compares the value of `x-director-passcode`, or the token of `Authorization: Bearer <token>` (scheme case-insensitive), with `crypto.timingSafeEqual` on equal-length buffers, and returns false on a length mismatch) and `registerMcp(app: Hono, deps: AppDeps, opts?: { service?: McpFilmService; env?: Env; log?: (line: Record<string, unknown>) => void }): void` (`AppDeps` as exported by S2; this is the signature the boot hook calls).

`registerMcp` adds `app.all('/mcp', handler)`. The handler returns HTTP 401 with the JSON body `{ jsonrpc: '2.0', error: { code: -32001, message: 'unauthorized' }, id: null }` when `checkPasscode` fails (and logs `mcp.auth.denied` without any header value). Otherwise it creates a new `McpServer({ name: 'pixitween-director', version: '1.0.0' })`, calls `registerFilmTools` with `opts?.service ?? makeDefaultService({ deps, env })`, creates a new `WebStandardStreamableHTTPServerTransport({ sessionIdGenerator: undefined, enableJsonResponse: true, maxRequestBodySize: 16 * 1024 * 1024, ... })`, calls `await server.connect(transport)`, returns `await transport.handleRequest(c.req.raw)` and closes the server in a `finally`.

Always pass `allowedHosts` (`localhost`, `localhost:<PORT>`, `127.0.0.1`, `127.0.0.1:<PORT>` and the host of `env.PUBLIC_BASE_URL`, which has a default in `loadEnv`) and `enableDnsRebindingProtection: true`.

Create server/mcp-server.test.ts with a bare Hono app, a fake service and the real SDK: a `Client` over `StreamableHTTPClientTransport(new URL('http://localhost/mcp'), { fetch: (url, init) => app.request(url.toString(), init), requestInit: { headers } })`.
acceptanceCriteria: With `DIRECTOR_PASSCODE='p'`, a `Client` using header `x-director-passcode: p` connects and `listTools` returns the 5 tool names; using `Authorization: Bearer p` also connects
A POST to `/mcp` with a wrong or missing passcode returns HTTP 401 and a body whose `error.message` is `unauthorized`; with `DIRECTOR_PASSCODE` unset it is accepted
A POST with `Accept: application/json` only (no `text/event-stream`) returns HTTP 406, and a POST whose `Host` header is `evil.example` is refused with a non-2xx status
`checkPasscode(new Headers({ 'x-director-passcode': 'ab' }), 'abc')` is false (length mismatch) and `checkPasscode(new Headers({ authorization: 'bearer abc' }), 'abc')` is true
`npm run typecheck` passes
`npm test` passes (offline, no network)
`npm run lint` passes

steps: Read docs/hackathon/steps/step-11-stretch/design.md section 9 (manual gate), docs/hackathon/06-contracts.md section 1 (the `scripts/live/<step>.ts` contract: `describe`, `estimateUsd`, `run`) and scripts/live/run.ts (the dispatcher) with one existing script under scripts/live/.

`runWithClient` calls `create_film` (aspect `16:9`), polls `get_film` every 10 seconds (through `opts.sleep`) up to `maxPolls` (default 30) until the status is `ready` or `failed` (throwing on `failed` and on running out of polls), then calls `edit_film` with `editMessage` and returns the summary. It reads `structuredContent` from each result and throws when a result has `isError`.

It never prints the passcode.
Create scripts/live/s11-mcp.test.ts testing `describe`, `estimateUsd` and `runWithClient` with a scripted fake client and a fake `sleep`.
acceptanceCriteria: `estimateUsd()` returns 0.25 and `describe()` mentions the word `estimate` or the dollar amount

metadata.standingRule: Offline-only PRD. Every story is implementable and verifiable with unit tests, recorded fixtures and the browser preview; nothing here spends money or needs network. Live and paid checks are listed in metadata.manualGates and run by the owner.
guardrails: Work offline. Tests use recorded fixtures and DIRECTOR_REPLAY=1. Never call Meta, Clippy, Ollama or any other network service from a story, a test or a script you run during a story. The only network use allowed is `npm install`.
Never commit, push, tag, publish to npm, deploy or change repository settings. autoCommit is off and the owner commits.

Never edit anything under node_modules/. The engine `reacthub-pixitweenjs` is a dependency: if it lacks something, add a row to ENGINE-NEEDS.md (what, where, proposed API, workaround, story) and use a workaround or set notes to 'blocked: engine'.
Edit only the files named in the story's steps, plus their tests. Files under shared/ are contracts (specs/hackathon/meta/06-contracts.md): change them only in a story that says so.
Never put keys, tokens, cookies or personal data in code, fixtures, logs or docs. Fixtures are redacted: no Authorization headers and no data: URLs longer than 200 characters.
No real brand names, logos or real people's likeness in prompts, fixtures or assets.
Record only real results. Never invent measurements, latencies, prices or test output.
Do not add a dependency that the story or 06-contracts.md does not name. If one is truly needed, say why in notes.
Debug output goes to debug/<step>/iteration-NN/ (gitignored). Only curated, redacted fixtures are committed, under fixtures/<step>/.

A step that would call a paid or live API is written as a script that prints an estimate and exits unless `--yes` is passed (`npm run live -- <step> --yes`, one file per step under scripts/live/). Create such scripts; never run them.
Pin @modelcontextprotocol/sdk to the v1 API (1.32.2). Never install or import @modelcontextprotocol/server, @modelcontextprotocol/client or @modelcontextprotocol/node.
server/boot.ts is an S2 file: US-011 may only add the registerMcp import and append ONE hook to `bootHooks` (a named shared edit). server/main.ts and every other S2 file are never edited.
Tool results and errors never contain secrets, the passcode, signed URLs, hostnames of rejected image URLs or raw exception messages. Logs never contain tool arguments.
Tests use in-memory transports and injected fetch, lookup, stores and agents; no test opens a real port or resolves a real DNS name.

ui: Verify in the browser (dev-browser skill or preview): `npm run dev`, open the page named in the story, confirm the stated behaviour, and record what you saw in `notes`

manualGates: MG-1: owner records the go/no-go by Tue 3 Nov 12:00 ET (Option A only if S0-S9 are green; Option B is no-go per design section 13).

MG-2: owner connects Muse Code with the config in docs/mcp.md, runs `/mcp` in a session, confirms the five tools list, and records Muse Code's settings file path and whether the x-director-passcode header is forwarded.
